title: Uniform generation and section bounds for projective ideals with fixed Hilbert polynomial
statement:
Fix $n\geq0$ and a numerical polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ (one taking integer values for all sufficiently large integers). There is an integer $m\geq1$, depending only on $n,P$, with the following property over every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $Z\to T$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated), and with Hilbert polynomial $P$ on every geometric fibre. Here the fibre polynomial is the eventual homogeneous-coordinate Hilbert function. Write $p:\mathbf P^n_T\to T$, $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_T}\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, $\mathcal O_Z(d)=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_T}(d)$, and $V_d=\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d$; twists are those of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For every $d\geq m$ the canonical sequence
$$0\longrightarrow p_*\mathcal I(d)\longrightarrow V_d\longrightarrow (pi)_*\mathcal O_Z(d)\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, its terms are finite locally free (locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_T$), and the last term has rank $P(d)$. This sequence and both direct-image terms commute with arbitrary base change $T'\to T$, with the ideal on $T'$ understood as the ideal of $Z_{T'}$. The evaluation map $p^*p_*\mathcal I(m)\otimes\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathcal I$ is surjective, as is the multiplication map $V_{d-m}\otimes p_*\mathcal I(m)\to p_*\mathcal I(d)$ for every $d\geq m$.

source.place: Tags 08AG (lemma-bound-quotients-free), 08A6 (lemma-m-regular-up), 08A7 (lemma-m-regular-multiply), 08A8 (lemma-m-regular-globally-generated); relative finitely presented formulation via cohomology and base change, perfect.tex Tag 0A1H (lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect). Grothendieck Expose 221, Theorem 2.1 and the conditions preceding Lemma 3.3.

proof.text: Apply the uniform field-fibre lemma to $n,P$, and choose its integer $m\geq1$ once for all bases. Each geometric fibre of the family is a closed subscheme of the specified projective space with coordinate polynomial $P$, so its ideal is coherent and $m$-regular. For every $d\geq m$, the same lemma gives vanishing of positive cohomology of $\mathcal O_{Z_{\bar t}}(d)$, surjective polynomial restriction, and dimension $P(d)$. These conclusions include $n=0$ and empty fibres.

source.place: Tags 08AG (lemma-bound-quotients-free), 08A6 (lemma-m-regular-up), 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0), and 01XT (lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring); uniform field consequence with the twisted ideal long exact sequence

proof.text: For a nonempty base $T$ and each $d\geq m$, choose any geometric point. The preceding dimension equality shows that $r=P(d)$ is a nonnegative integer; the fibre lemma gives the same dimension at every geometric point. Apply the relative section-sequence lemma with this $d,r$: its hypotheses are precisely flat finite presentation of $Z/T$ and the three fibre assertions of step 1. It supplies the finite-type ideal, its canonical pullback as the actual base-changed ideal, the locally split restriction sequence, finite local freeness and rank, and canonical arbitrary base change for all its terms. For empty $T$ all sheaves and maps are zero, and the stated conditions hold vacuously.

source.place: Tags 0B9S (lemma-open-where-cohomology-in-degree-i-rank-r-geometric), 0B91 (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), 01XT (lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring); flat-closed-family ideal base change and split-kernel argument from the returned proof, steps 1, 4--6

proof.text: For nonempty $T$, apply the relative generation lemma with this same $m$. The ideal and its fibre identifications, and the locally free $K_b=p_*\mathcal I(b)$ with canonical geometric-fibre section isomorphisms for all $b\geq m$, are furnished by step 2. Step 1 supplies coherent $m$-regular fibre ideals. The lemma therefore gives the required evaluation surjection and every polynomial multiplication surjection. These and the sequences of step 2 are exactly the asserted conclusions. The choice of $m$ used only $n,P$.
